subject: Week 33: gift-debris sweep — button batteries are the top hazard

content.hook: gift-debris sweep — button batteries are the top hazard
content.thisWeek: Avi hits day 229 in peak holiday mode: expect long babble strings ("mamamama," "bababababa") — a CDC 9-month checkpoint item — plus raking food with his fingers and hunting for objects you hide. Many babies crawl in this stretch, though the CDC dropped crawling from its checklist entirely — some skip it and go straight to pulling to stand, which is emerging for early movers (CDC checkpoint: 12 months). Stranger anxiety runs at full strength through 7-10 months, so expect clinginess with rotating holiday visitors.
watchFors: [low concern] Clinginess and one-parent preference around holiday visitors — stranger anxiety peaks 7-10 months; give him warm-up time in your arms before hand-offs.
[low concern] Sleep disruption for 1-3 nights around travel or late gatherings — protect the usual bedtime where you can.
[monitor] Upper-respiratory cluster after extended-family contact — track fever, feeding, and breathing effort rather than counting days.
[call within 24h] Persistent illness that is not improving, or any new wheezing.

[call now] Suspected button-battery or magnet ingestion from new toys or gift debris — ER immediately, do not wait for symptoms; fever ≥102°F (rectal) with lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips — 911.

enrichment.body: Run a floor-level sweep before and after gift-opening: ribbons, coin batteries, small ornaments, and loose battery compartments on new toys are the season's ingestion hazards.

Put raking-size finger foods on the tray daily — puffs, banana pieces, well-cooked lentils. Raking is the CDC 9-month item; the two-finger pincer it feeds is checked at 12 months. Featuring iron-rich options now also sets up the hemoglobin rescreen at the 9-month visit.
Answer his babble strings as conversation — pause, respond, wait for the return serve. Conversational turns, not word count alone, predict language-network development (Romeo et al. 2018).
Cap the schedule at one major event per day and hold naps fixed — an overtired evening collapse costs more than any gathering delivers.

upcoming: Day 235 (Jan 1, 2027): New Year's — he will be asleep at midnight; keep bedtime and log it as a parents-only marker.
Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — book it now for early in the window; iron rescreen, influenza #2 if first season, and possibly an ASQ-3 developmental screen.

subject: Week 34: book the 9-month visit — iron rescreen and ASQ-3 ahead

content.hook: book the 9-month visit — iron rescreen and ASQ-3 ahead
content.thisWeek: This is the CDC 9-month checklist in live action: getting to sitting on his own, transferring objects hand to hand, raking food, varied babble strings, and reacting when you leave the room. The well-visit window opens Day 252 (Jan 18) — the pediatrician will run a hemoglobin rescreen and often a standardized ASQ-3 developmental screen, so book now and start a notes file: babble variety, feeding, sleep, anything that nags at you.
watchFors: [low concern] Shyness or fear around strangers and lifting arms to be picked up — both are on-schedule 9-month social behavior.
[monitor] No babble strings, no response to his name, or no object transfer between hands — none is an emergency, all belong in the visit notes.
[call within 24h] New wheezing, or an illness that stops improving after day three.
[call now] Fever ≥102°F (rectal) with lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips — call now or 911.

enrichment.body: Lock the paid swim slot before the conversion window closes Wednesday Jan 6: La Petite Baleen runs perpetual enrollment at $130-138/mo, or check JCCSF Water Babies for openings (waitlists cap at five). One program only — there is no dose-response evidence under 12 months.
Play object-permanence games daily: hide a toy under a cup, pause, reveal. Looking for hidden objects is the 9-month cognitive checkpoint, and predictable surprise is the engagement mechanism.
Read 30 min/day but slow down: pause after he vocalizes and respond as if it were a word — that serve-and-return loop is the active ingredient.
Rehearse short separations with a fixed ritual — same phrase, brief exit, prompt return. Separation protest is object permanence applied to people; predictable exits shrink it.

upcoming: Day 240 (Jan 6, 2027): paid-swim conversion window closes — last day to hold the queue position.
Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — book this week to land early in the window; influenza #2 if this is his first flu season, iron rescreen, possible ASQ-3.

subject: Week 35: anchor the furniture — pulling to stand changes the risk map

content.hook: anchor the furniture — pulling to stand changes the risk map
content.thisWeek: Receptive language is running ahead of production: he likely understands 10-20 simple words, and production typically lags reception by 1-3 months. Cruising along furniture is consolidating for early movers and pulling to stand keeps improving — both are CDC 12-month checkpoints, so later is still normal. The same cognitive upgrade that finds hidden toys now notices exits, which is why separation protest and a sleep wobble often arrive together around 8-9 months.
watchFors: [low concern] More night wakings and bedtime protest without illness — the 8-9-month sleep disruption typically resolves in 2-4 weeks and often overlaps the shift from three naps to two.
[low concern] Falls and bumps during cruising practice — pad sharp corners and keep practice zones on forgiving surfaces.
[monitor] No pulling to stand or cruising yet — not a red flag (CDC checkpoint: 12 months), but worth a line in the 9-month visit notes.
[call within 24h] Sudden persistent sleep refusal arriving with illness signs — fever, ear-pulling, refusing feeds.
[call now] Head injury followed by persistent vomiting or lethargy; fever ≥102°F (rectal) with lethargy; labored breathing or blue lips — 911.

enrichment.body: Anchor everything tall this week — TV, dressers, bookshelves — and hardware-mount a gate at the top of any stairs. Pulling to stand converts furniture from scenery into load-bearing equipment, and tip-overs are a recurring, preventable cause of infant deaths.
Hold the bedtime routine absolutely fixed through the regression: same sequence, same brief response at wakings. Consistency is the intervention; novelty resets the clock.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP: Getting Your Baby to Sleep

enrichment.body: Sing hand-motion songs — Itsy Bitsy Spider, pat-a-cake — imitation, rhythm, and receptive vocabulary in one activity; pat-a-cake itself is a CDC 1-year checklist item some babies show early.
Ask two-choice questions at the book — where is the dog, here or here. He answers with gaze before he answers with a point, and both count as comprehension data for the ASQ-3.

upcoming: Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — window opens in nine days; if it is not booked, book it today.
Day 250-256 (Jan 16-22, 2027): first-step territory opens for early walkers (full range 9-17 months) — clear the cruising runways now.

subject: Week 36: 9-month visit window opens Monday — first steps for some

content.hook: 9-month visit window opens Monday — first steps for some
content.thisWeek: First-step territory opens for early walkers this week — the full range runs 9-17 months, and the CDC moved its walks-alone checkpoint to 15 months, so later is not a lag. Expect brief unsupported stands for some, functional object use (cup to mouth, phone to ear), and possibly a first specific word: mama or dada aimed at the right parent. The 9-month well-visit window opens Monday Jan 18.
watchFors: [low concern] Falls rise as cruising speeds up — the standard is supervised falls onto forgiving surfaces, not zero falls.
[low concern] Everything still goes in the mouth — keep the daily floor sweep going.
[monitor] Babble that stays vowel-only, without consonant variety — raise it at this month's visit.
[call within 24h] Persistent illness that is not improving.
[call now] Fever ≥102°F (rectal) with lethargy; labored breathing or blue lips — 911.

enrichment.body: Practice walking his way: hold both hands and let him step, or set a weighted push toy along the cruising route. Keep him barefoot indoors — bare feet beat shoes for early balance; save soft soles for outdoor surfaces.

Decide the Suzuki question before the option lapses Feb 5: pick the instrument (violin, piano, or cello), start Book 1 recordings 30+ min/day, and join named-teacher waitlists — top SF teachers run multi-year lists, so listing now targets a 2029-2030 lesson start. Cost today: recordings only.
Play give-and-take: ask for the toy with an open hand, thank him, hand it back. Giving objects on request sits on the CDC 1-year checklist and doubles as turn-taking rehearsal.
Shift reading toward retrieval practice — name an image and let him find it on the page. Pointing on request is exactly what the ASQ-3 samples.

upcoming: Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — window opens Monday; iron rescreen, influenza #2 if first season, possible ASQ-3. Bring the notes file: babble variety, feeding, sleep, mobility.
Day 270 (Feb 5, 2027): Suzuki teacher-waitlist and ISR instructor-contact windows both close — ISR decision detail next week.

subject: Week 37: pincer practice at every meal — open cup beats the sippy

content.hook: pincer practice at every meal — open cup beats the sippy
content.thisWeek: The pincer grasp — thumb and index finger — is emerging and refines fastest with daily practice; the CDC checks it at 12 months, so emerging now is ahead of the checkpoint, not a requirement. Self-feeding capacity is expanding: many infants this week can drink from an open cup with help, which beats a sippy for oral-motor development. Babble is picking up adult-like intonation, and a specific mama or dada is emerging for some.
watchFors: [low concern] Food and objects launched from the high chair — gravity experimentation, not defiance; it fades faster without an audience reaction.
[monitor] No raking grasp or no progress toward picking up small foods — bring it to the 9-month visit.
[monitor] Not imitating sounds or simple actions — same route: visit notes, not alarm.
[call within 24h] Persistent illness that is not improving.
[call now] Choking with no air movement — start infant back blows and chest thrusts and call 911; fever ≥102°F (rectal) with lethargy — call now.

enrichment.body: Serve two-finger-size pieces at every meal and hand over pre-loaded spoons (yogurt, mashed potato). The mess is the training signal — daily self-feeding practice drives the pincer refinement the CDC checks at 12 months.
Offer an open cup with help at one meal a day and sketch the bottle exit: AAP guidance is off bottles entirely by 12 months, and open-cup practice is the ramp.

Contact certified ISR instructors before the window closes Feb 5 if pool or regular water exposure is in the family's future — Bay Area instructors book 6-12+ months out, and the evidence is case-series only, so treat it as drowning-risk mitigation, not enrichment.

Keep live music daily — sing the same two songs at cleanup and bath. Active participation, not playback, is what moved pitch discrimination and prelinguistic gesture in the randomized trial (Gerry, Unrau and Trainor 2012).

Day 270 (Feb 5, 2027): ISR instructor-contact and Suzuki-waitlist windows close.
Day 264-270 (Jan 30–Feb 5, 2027): first words consolidating — log anything that sounds referential.
